claims.text: The nanoparticles contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios.
The multi-metal nanoparticles initially have a crystalline solid-solution state.
A stable solid-solution crystalline state maintains the structural stability of the nanoparticles from 473 to 1923 K.
A stable solid-solution crystalline state maintains the chemical stability of the nanoparticles from 473 to 1923 K.
High entropy of mixing governs formation or persistence of the stable solid solution.
High entropy of mixing reduces the free energy of the system.
The reduction in free energy stabilizes the solid-solution crystalline state.
The nanoparticles will maintain structural and chemical stability under catalytic and thermoelectric operating conditions across 473–1923 K.
High-throughput density-functional theory calculations can simulate the behavior of these alloys at different temperatures and operating conditions.
In situ X-ray diffraction, transmission electron microscopy, and energy-dispersive spectroscopy can assess structural and chemical stability under high-temperature conditions.
Significant degradation or phase separation under high-temperature operating conditions would falsify the proposed stability mechanism.
